long_biography.plain_text:
An Antarctic ski traverse turned Emmanuelle Dumas from an experienced land-based guide into an expedition sailor. She arrived aboard with no sailing background and persistent seasickness, then accumulated more than 60,000 nautical miles between Cape Horn and the high Arctic. The shift joined her mountain skills to Christophe Votat's seafaring experience and made remote coasts accessible to travellers.

Dumas builds each itinerary around conditions rather than a fixed route, moving between navigation and shore expeditions as weather and ice allow. More than fifteen years of professional guiding underpin that approach. She also records remote landscapes through magazine writing and watercolour, continuing to document the places in which she works.
